rubric.why: Awards credit for recognizing sabotage as intentional harmful action.
rubric.how: Look for wording that indicates the action is intentional.

rubric.why: Awards credit for identifying the computer or network target.
rubric.description: Identifies what sabotage harms or disrupts.
rubric.how: Look for a computer system, data, or network as the target.

modelAnswer: Sabotage is the deliberate damage or disruption of a computer system, data, or network.

items.followUp: What is the function of the network layer?

rubric.why: Recognizes that the data link layer handles data in frames.
rubric.description: Identifies frames as the data unit handled by the layer.
rubric.how: Look for the term “frames” or an equivalent description of data units.

rubric.why: Recognizes a key link-level function between connected devices.
rubric.description: States a function such as delivery between adjacent nodes, error detection, or physical addressing.
rubric.how: Award for any one listed function.

modelAnswer: The data link layer organizes data into frames for transmission over a link.
It provides node-to-node delivery and may handle physical addressing and error detection.

rubric.why: Identifies control information as information carried with data.
rubric.description: States that control information is information or instructions.

rubric.why: Shows that this information helps manage or interpret data communication.
rubric.description: States a control purpose, such as managing transmission or identifying source/destination.
rubric.how: Award for a relevant control purpose.

modelAnswer: Control information is information added to data to help manage its communication.
It may identify the source or destination or help control transmission and error checking.

items.followUp: What is the advantage of software sharing in a network?

rubric.why: Identifies the central advantage: network users can share hardware.
rubric.description: States that hardware can be shared by network users.
rubric.how: Look for hardware or devices being shared.

rubric.why: Explains a practical benefit of sharing hardware.
rubric.description: States that sharing saves cost or gives users access to common devices.
rubric.how: Look for reduced expense or an example such as a shared printer.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing allows several users on a network to use the same devices, such as a printer or scanner.
It reduces the cost of buying a separate device for every user.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a client and a server.

rubric.why: Checks that the sender's role is correctly stated.
rubric.description: States that the sender sends or transmits data or a message.
rubric.how: Look for the sender’s sending role.

rubric.why: Checks that the receiver's role is correctly stated.
rubric.description: States that the receiver gets data or a message.
rubric.how: Look for the receiver’s receiving role.

modelAnswer: Sender: The device or person that sends a message or data.
Receiver: The device or person that receives the message or data.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm? Name two things identified when analysing a problem before drawing its flowchart.

rubric.why: Checks that a flowchart is described as a visual representation using symbols.
rubric.description: Defines a flowchart as a graphical or diagrammatic representation of a solution or algorithm.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its visual form and representation of steps or a solution.

rubric.why: Input is one of the requirements identified during problem analysis.
Checks for another requirement used to plan the flowchart.
rubric.description: Identifies processing, output, decisions, or the sequence of steps.
rubric.how: Award for any one of these requirements.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm or solution, using standard symbols to show its steps.
To determine its requirements, analyse the problem and identify the inputs and the processing needed.
Identify the required outputs and any decisions or conditions.
Arrange the steps in the correct sequence before drawing the flowchart.
